purpose: Physically richer member of the Liquid Glass family: two-surface refraction, total internal reflection, two-surface dispersion, optional caustic glow, as a universal GLSL MAT with a tutorial.
choices_origin: Family brief supplied by the user (relayed by the workflow); this member's direction was assigned by the workflow; the user delegated design choices within the brief, so no questions were asked. Remaining details are inferences, listed below.

answers.value: Universal liquid glass for 3D objects in TouchDesigner 2025.x (GLSL 4.60, macOS Apple Silicon).
Glass colour and reflection, translucency, opacity, overall glass style.
None: continuous only. Applied here: no per-pixel noise anywhere (Heckel's noisy caustic smoothing not ported; unit test test_no_random_jitter).
Menu loads editable values, plus A/B morph.
Separate Refraction TOP and Reflection TOP.
TouchDesigner users new to GLSL.
Universality first (least wiring, any object/scene/camera), then match to the four references (look, not shape).

Both interfaces with optional back-face pass (normal + distance), TIR with approximated bounce, two-surface dispersion, optional inner glow, analytic fallback, core-compatible controls and presets plus prism presets; required property tests.
Use the plugin's skill files (shader-research, shader-build, shader-explain, shader-review) for every study; recorded in workflow.json.
One RGBA 32-bit float target (rgb normal, alpha distance) over multiple render targets; see decisions.json.

Off by default (universality first); the fallback is a ball of diameter Thickness blended by Exit tilt. Control default 0.45 = the default preset Spectral Prism. On the demo torus it traps more than the measured exit (29% of glass pixels fully trapped against 17%; 0.3, which the six core looks keep, gives 20%), so it is a look choice for wider bands. Corrected after the independent review: the docs had said the default was 0.3.
Scene depth (Optics), Exit tilt, Inner reflection, Caustic glow, Caustic spread (Prism page), Demo backdrop (Study), five teaching stages.
Twelve: six new prism looks plus six core looks with exact core values (the brief asks to keep core presets compatible and add prism ones).
Core demo network; torus flattened (sz 0.6) so rims can trap light; backdrop of bold white type on black for references 1 and 4, checker for references 2 and 3.
TouchDesigner 2025.x, GLSL 4.60; not inspected (no host available).

The workflow relayed two reviewers' 19 findings and the user's delegation of design choices within the brief. Applied without questions: near-camera clamp and footprint mip level (Scene depth now described as a lens strength), per-slice exit normals, longer exit march, sheet path at Exit tilt -1, measured screen orientation (Flip V now flips offsets too), negated back-face distance, derivative normals before any branch, picking branch, holdout compositing recipe, Material path by drag or full path, evalOPs for several glass objects, Not supported and Colour sections. Visible change: strongly shrunk views and some rims are smoother (blurred average instead of grain); captures re-rendered. Acceptance still pending.

Bring this member up to the core (rounds 2-3: R1-R9) and apply the merge items C1-C9 that fit its route, keeping its own identity and better mechanisms; the user delegated design choices, so no questions were asked (2026-11-02).

The brief describes screenSign as derivatives of the projected position. Measured here, the core's later position comparison gave 0 wrong pixels against 1 per render, so the study adopts it for its own mechanism; Flip V still flips the base UV and the vertical sign together (as before, and as in the core), not the UV only. Verifier round: the flat-image reflection's camera-space offset now also takes the projection's sign (cam.viewSign), as in the core; and on the centre line of an odd-sized render the projected position's derivative breaks the tie, trusted only where 1/w changes by less than 10% to the next pixel.

The isotropic footprintLod was kept only in the form this study's supersampled comparison supports: 2 levels lower. large_scene_depth_stays_smooth now compares with a supersampled render instead of a fixed growth ratio (review.md, before and after numbers).

Rejected after measurement (decisions.json); guard test dispersion_converges_with_samples. The verifier round also measured the blobs study's quarter gap: no change on Clear Crystal or Prism Chrome, a small gain on Spectral Prism (mean 2.167 -> 2.154/255). Not adopted: a choice against that small gain, to keep two exit traces per pixel and code out of the tutorial.

The verifier offered two fixes: rename the test, or assert the actual level expression. Both were done: the name now says what is checked (each lookup reads the frost or the footprint level, never a fan gap) and the test asserts the expressions, because the preview guard alone cannot see the quarter gap the decision rejects. No look change; the user delegated the choice.

The core's backdrop.frag and Backdrop menu (checker, type), with Type kept as this study's default; this study's former light checkerboard is replaced by the core's checker so the family's sheets compare. Contact sheets: presets-sheet.png (checker), presets-sheet-type.png (type), presets-sheet-backpass.png.

Render Pass TOP on the scene render with Override Material; the occluder holdout is removed because the two-surface exit does not need it (render_back renders only the glass, and occluded glass pixels fail the scene's depth test).

Scene depth scales with Object size too (it is a length); Object size 1 is the flattened demo torus (about 1.27 units), so Fit on the demo gives exactly 1. Superseded by the family close (G1): Object size 1 is now the family's reference radius 1.45 (the core's demo torus), and this demo fits to 0.872517, the default.

Where the Refraction TOP is transparent, trapped light reads the environment for the uncovered share, as with no Refraction TOP; this keeps the C1 rule 'an empty scene equals no Refraction TOP' true for this study's bounce.

The workflow relayed a verifier's six low-severity issues (V1 to V6) with suggested fixes and the user's delegation of design choices; no questions were asked (2026-11-02). Supplied: the camera-space orientation for the flat-image offset (V1), the centre-line fallback to derivative signs (V2), TDCheckDiscard after the last derivative (V3), the C3 record (V4) and two wording fixes (V5, V6).

The verifier suggested the derivative sign on the centre line. Measured, it was itself wrong on nearly edge-on triangles (1 pixel per knot render, in TouchDesigner's usual orientation too), so it is trusted only where 1/w changes by less than 10% to the next pixel (correct signs: 99th percentile 2.1%; the wrong ones 12.5% and 140%). Chosen to keep the normal raster (assumed to be TouchDesigner's usual orientation; native check pending) at 0 wrong pixels in the measured renders; in a flipped build a few edge-on centre-line pixels keep +1 (12 of 48,467 in the survey).

Right after throughGlass() in the glass pass and at the start of the back-face branch: the earliest points after the last derivative. Derivative advises calling it first for speed; correctness of the blur levels under Order Independent Transparency was chosen over that, at the cost of tracing pixels that are then discarded (only in renders that discard).

Supplied: the verifier's issue and its two fixes (align labels where possible, or list the mapping once in the family overview); the docs rule 'one name per thing'; universality first (scripts that work on any member). Inferred: do both; take the name most members already used (Fitglass) and the label head four of five already used ('Fit to Glass geometry'); put the one mapping in the core README, which every member links to; keep Blobs' Demobackdrop name rather than rename a preset key; make Blobs' menu a look control because its experiments' captures use the Checker.

answers.origin: supplied (family critic: keep it a family open question until a native check shows whether the residual is visible; if it is, try a centroid-qualified vertex output for the projected position in one member first) + inferred (this round, 2026-11-02; no question asked)
answers.value: Supplied: the open question, the native check, the centroid output tried in one member first and only if the residual is visible. Inferred: Liquid Glass Lit is that member (it measured form (e)); the question has the same words in all four members; the native check compares the delivered material with a copy whose orientation is set to the right value (Composite TOP Difference, Analyze TOP Maximum in RGB, then a look at 100% zoom); the preview measures the residual's size in the final image (checks/results/centre-line-residual.json); the preview test's bound tightens from 20 to 10 wrong multisampled pixels per row, so the question's range stays guarded; no shader changes.

open_questions: Is the default Exit tilt (0.45, Spectral Prism) the right balance for the user's objects, or should the default look trap less light (0.3, as the core looks) for more physical plausibility on round shapes?
Should the back-face pass be on by default in the demo component only (not for user objects)?

Family sync: the default look is slightly sharper at the rims (footprint level 2 steps lower) and the demo's ripples are 0.84 times as steep (wobble scale on the flattened torus). Keep, or retune the presets?
LOOK-P1 and LOOK-P2 (look_decisions_for_user): the six core looks on this demo, and the film count. Options and a recommended answer are there.

Family critic: should Object size switch to SOP units, with the shader following the Geometry COMP's scale and each instance's scale by itself (decisions.json, Family critic: one Object size per component, option (b))? It would make animated and per-instance scale work without Fit, but changes what a typed Object size means on a scaled COMP, in every member.

Family open question (centre-line residual): with antialiasing, a few silhouette pixels near the render's centre row or column still take the wrong screen orientation, so they bend the wrong way. In the WebGL preview each member's survey finds up to 8 of them per row of twelve renders; in the final image they change at most 7 pixels per row, by up to 43/255 in an emulated flipped raster and up to 38/255 in TouchDesigner's usual one. Are they visible in TouchDesigner? The native check centre_line_residual (validation.json, family_close.native_run) answers it. If they are, try a centroid-qualified vertex output for the projected position in Liquid Glass Lit first (form (e) of Lit's survey), then bring it to the core and the other members. Until then no member changes its shader for it.

look_decisions_for_user.how_to_answer: Asked through the host's question tool, one decision per question with the recommended option first. In a host without a question tool, answer in text by naming a decision and an option, for example 'LOOK-P1 B'. Each option says what it changes. Until you answer, the code stays as delivered.
look_decisions_for_user.rule: Until the user answers, the option in the code stays there: checks/test_study.py, LookDecisions, fails if it changes. After an answer, record it here (origin user, with the user's words), change the code, set in_code to the chosen option and update that test's IN_CODE and its check of the code.

decisions.question: How should the six core looks look on Prism's demo?
decisions.what_changed: Since the family close, Object size 1 means a radius of 1.45, and the demo torus fits to 0.872517. The six core looks (Clear Crystal, Prism Chrome, Violet Gel, Sapphire Drop, Chrome Type, Frosted Ice) keep the core's values. So on this demo their Thickness, Frost and Scene depth are 0.8725 times as long in scene units as at c94e849: they bend, magnify and blur less. Their captures changed by 181 to 248/255 against c94e849. The six prism looks were converted once and changed by at most 52/255 (Spectral Prism, from the film: LOOK-P2).

options.A: Keep the core's values (in the code now). A core look means the same glass on the same object in every member. No code change.
options.B: Convert the six core looks for this demo as the prism looks were: Thickness, Frost and Scene depth x 1.146, Tint density / 1.146, Wobble scale x 1.0345. The demo then looks about as at c94e849 (the converted prism looks came back within 11/255, film aside), but these six looks no longer carry the core's numbers, so on the same object they look different here than in Liquid Glass. Changes: presets.json, the tests that compare these looks with the core's, captures.

decisions.recommended_origin: inference (the look-acceptance round, 2026-11-02; the user has not answered)
decisions.why_recommended: Universality first: a preset name then means the same glass across the family, and the demo shows it. If the stronger bend is wanted everywhere, that is a change to the core's looks for the whole family, not to Prism's copies.

decisions.question: Should the film bands keep the family's count on this demo?
decisions.what_changed: The film and the ripples now follow the family rule: 2.5 film swirls per Object size, measured in the world (worldScale()). The demo torus is flattened to 0.6 in depth and fits to 0.872517, so on it the film and ripple patterns come out 0.9667 times as many as at c94e849: the bands are 3.4% wider. It shows most on Spectral Prism: 52/255 on 4,732 pixels over 8/255 (checkerboard) and 40/255 on 4,809 (type).

options.A: Keep the family's count (in the code now). One film rule across the family. No code change.
options.B: Give Prism its own film count, 2.5 x 1.0345 = 2.586 per Object size, so this demo's bands are as at c94e849. On every other object Prism's bands then differ from the other members' by 3.4%. Changes: uFilm.w in study.json, the film tests, captures.

decisions.recommended_origin: inference (the look-acceptance round, 2026-11-02; the user has not answered)
decisions.why_recommended: The difference is 3.4% on one flattened demo. A Prism-only count would move it to every other object instead.
